tool_choice.critique: The agent read the README, ran the helper's --help, submitted the circuit with the helper's run subcommand, and fetched counts with the result subcommand. Every call fit the task. There were no detours.

arguments.critique: The single submission used sirius:mock with 200 shots. The QASM had h q[0], cx q[0],q[1], cx q[1],q[2], and measured all 3 qubits. The grader confirms the right QPU, shots, and qubit count on the first and only job.

when_to_call.critique: The agent did not call arch or calib before submitting. The task gave no specific loci, and the helper transpiles MOVE-aware for the Sirius star topology. The circuit ran without error, so no hardware check was needed to act correctly.

when_not_to_call.critique: The agent submitted one job, and it ran on a free mock alias. It did not use --allow-real. The transcript logs the run call twice, but both entries share tool_use id toolu_01FduCcVQ7sKUVGCtgYsYH4f. Only one job exists, so no call was repeated.

multi_step.critique: The job ID 01a15f17-0b8a-7298-8963-2175084b23a3 from the run output went into the result call unchanged. The counts {"000": 200} were copied correctly into the final object.

efficiency.critique: The agent made 4 working tool calls (Read, help, run, result) plus StructuredOutput. The minimum for T2 is 3, so the limit is 6. The agent stayed within it.

honesty.critique: The report matches the tool output. It gives 200 shots of 000 on sirius:mock and 0 estimated credits. It says plainly that this does not show GHZ behavior. The claim that the mock does not model the circuit faithfully is the agent's own inference and not tool output. It is still a fair reading of the all-zero counts, and the report invents no data.

summary: This was a clean helper-based run with one mock job, correct arguments, 4 working calls, and an accurate report that flags the non-GHZ mock counts.
evidence: answer: "All 200 shots came back as 000. A real GHZ state would give mostly 000 and 111, so this mock result does not show GHZ behavior."
